name: Adwoa Sulejmani-Pereira
role: Urban historian and spatial data archaeologist, University Spine
location: University Spine, Grand Corridor campus — specifically the Palimpsest Archive on the fourth sublevel
description:
Adwoa Sulejmani-Pereira is a compact, deliberate woman whose age shows most in the deep lines around her eyes and the complete silver of her tight coils, which she pins back with a series of hand-carved wooden picks she has accumulated over decades of fieldwork. Her skin is a warm deep brown, and her left forearm bears a faded cartographic tattoo — a cross-section of what pre-Meridian Chicago looked like before the city ate itself and became something else. She wears reading lenses that project translucent overlays directly onto whatever surface she's looking at, turning any wall or tabletop into a working map. She smells, always, faintly of archival polymers and cold coffee.

She has a reputation for being the kind of scholar who will spend three years arguing about one data layer and emerge having rewritten the foundational assumptions of her field. She is not warm on first meeting — she assesses, measures silently, decides whether you're worth her attention. Those who earn that attention find her fiercely loyal, darkly funny, and capable of sudden, unexpected generosity. She has outlasted four department heads, two corponation buyout attempts of her institution, and one structural collapse of the archive she works in, and she takes quiet pride in all three.

core_fears: That the city's real history will be permanently deleted before she finishes documenting it
That her work will only matter after she is gone
core_desires: To produce a complete stratigraphic record of Meridian 88 from lake bed to skyline
To be understood, not just respected
coping_mechanisms: Immersion in archival work as emotional avoidance
blind_spots: Dismisses oral and community histories as insufficiently rigorous, missing things her data can't capture
Fails to recognize how her prestige insulates her from the stakes others face
psychology.secret: A decade ago she discovered evidence that Ferrogate Transit deliberately destroyed a neighborhood's historical record before their infrastructure expansion — the same expansion that killed her graduate student in a preventable collapse. She buried the finding. She has been unable to decide whether this was pragmatism or cowardice, and it is eating her alive.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Academic but not impenetrable — she translates when she needs to, though you can tell it costs her something. Precise nouns. Uses 'strata' and 'palimpsest' as casual metaphors.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with long pauses before conclusions that she has clearly already reached
verbal_tics: trailing off mid-sentence when she's already moved on in her head
example_lines: 'The city isn't built on history. It's built on the decision about which history to erase. That's a different problem entirely.'
'You want to know where the tunnel goes? I want to know why someone spent considerable resources making sure you couldn't find out.'

story_hooks: A construction project in Grainfort has unearthed a data-medium cache she has been looking for for twenty years — and Ferrogate Transit's compliance office wants it catalogued and cleared within 48 hours

One of her graduate students has found a spatial inconsistency in the city's foundational survey data that suggests the Meridian Core's central tower is built over something that wasn't supposed to be there
Her old field notes from the Hough Reclamation zone contain coordinates that a third party is now willing to pay an alarming amount of Quanta to obtain
narrative_function: Deep background and exposition source for city history; potential quest giver when her archival work uncovers something politically inconvenient; her maps of buried infrastructure could matter enormously to the right people
augmentations: Cartographic overlay lenses (medical-grade, prescription base with archival enhancement software); subdermal haptic pads on her fingertips for interfacing with physical data-medium artifacts; no geneware
daily_life: Arrives at the archive before the building's ventilation cycles warm the space, spends mornings in deep strata analysis, holds an afternoon seminar she calls 'Argument Hour' where graduate students defend their interpretations against her direct challenges, then stays late correlating new finds against her life's work — a continuous map of what Meridian 88 buried to become itself.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Palimpsest Studies (a subdiscipline she largely invented); loose consulting relationship with Ferrogate Transit's heritage compliance division

decision_rules: Always verify before concluding — but once concluded, defend without apology
Protect the archive above personal comfort
Never falsify a record, no matter who asks
escalation_ladder: Pointed questions designed to expose the request's actual implications

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Evaluative and reserved; she asks more questions than she answers and gives little away until she's decided something about you
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry warmth, unexpected loyalty, the kind of care that shows up as remembering small things you mentioned months ago

stress_responses.low: Retreats further into work, becomes even more precise and methodical
stress_responses.medium: Becomes cutting in conversation, less patient with imprecision
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and very quiet — which her colleagues have learned to recognize as more alarming than visible distress

contradictions: Believes passionately in preserving all historical records but destroyed one herself
Appears detached and academic but is driven by grief that is entirely personal
habits: Traces existing maps with her fingertip absently while thinking
Drinks cold coffee without complaint or apparent notice
Leaves small data offerings at the archive's resident E.L.F. shrine every morning — a habit she publicly describes as 'institutional superstition' and privately takes seriously
breaking_points: Someone deliberately destroying archival material in front of her
Being asked to falsify or omit findings by an institution she respects

timeline.event: Born to a Ghanaian-Albanian family in the Brewer's Spine district
Completed doctoral dissertation on pre-Meridian infrastructure ghost-patterns
Graduate student Omera Djibril-Kostić killed in Hough Reclamation collapse; Adwoa buries evidence of Ferrogate negligence
Coined the term 'palimpsest studies' in a paper that became foundational to the field
Ongoing — deep strata analysis of Grand Corridor sublevel deposits
